Metadata.title: Oleksandra Kokozei | UI/UX Designer & Design Engineer
Metadata.description: Portfolio of Oleksandra Kokozei, a UI/UX designer and design engineer based in Stuttgart, Germany.

bio.p1: I’m a UI/UX designer who loves the space where aesthetics, logic, and technology meet. I’m naturally curious and detail-obsessed, and I enjoy turning messy ideas into clear, intuitive experiences that feel effortless to use.
bio.p2: I love not only designing ideas, but bringing them to life which led me to explore AI engineering and turn concepts into functional digital experiences. I learn by making, experimenting, and asking too many “what if?” questions.
bio.p3: At heart, I’m equal parts visual thinker, problem-solver, and curious builder with a soft spot for thoughtful details.

ces.description: CES’s administration platform connects recruitment workflows for crewing companies with the internal management of seafarer records, documents, and services. My UX/UI scope covers both CRM environments, focusing on information structure, operational workflows, and interfaces for managing interconnected records.
ces.coverAlt: Calm sea at dusk with the white CES logo in the center

overview.label: Overview
overview.body:
My work centers on the operational interfaces used by crewing companies and the CES team. Both environments connect to the same maritime ecosystem, but each serves a different set of daily tasks.
Crewing managers need to publish vacancies, review applications, find suitable seafarers, and manage communication. The CES team needs to maintain seafarer records, process verification and service requests, oversee crewing companies, and moderate vacancies.

The design challenge is to give each team a focused workspace while making the relationships between people, documents, vacancies, and requests clear.

scope.label: Scope
scope.lead: From recruitment management to platform operations.

crewingCrm.title: Crewing CRM
crewingCrm.body:
The recruitment workspace covers vacancy management, application review, seafarer search, candidate records, and messaging. Its scope also includes company information, manager administration, recruitment statistics, and notifications.
A key consideration is the vacancy lifecycle: distinguishing listings awaiting moderation from published, closed, and archived vacancies, while keeping applications and candidate actions accessible.

cesCrm.title: CES CRM
cesCrm.body:
The internal workspace covers seafarer records, document verification, service requests, crewing companies, and vacancy moderation. Supporting areas include reference data such as ranks and availability, news, statistics, and activity history.
The seafarer profile brings together professional information, availability, the assigned manager, documents, services, and order history. It also provides access to bonus records, invoicing, and CV generation, making it a central point for multiple operational tasks.

wireframes.caption: Initial CRM wireframes
wireframes.alt: Grid of early wireframes for the Crewing CRM and CES CRM: record pages, data tables, filters and forms

workflows.label: Workflows
workflows.lead: Designing the connections between records and actions.

vacancies.title: Vacancies and applications
vacancies.body: A vacancy connects a role and vessel with employment details, publication status, and applications. The interface needs to support both an overview of recruitment activity and the review of individual listings and candidates.

seafarers.title: Seafarers and documents
seafarers.body: A seafarer record connects professional details and availability with supporting documents. Document validity and verification require distinct status information so that administrators can understand what is current, what needs review, and what requires follow-up.

services.title: Services and orders
services.body:
Service requests connect a seafarer with a specific task, its progress, and related order or payment information. Administrators need enough context to continue processing a request without losing track of the person or records involved.
Across these workflows, my design focus is clear hierarchy, searchable and filterable lists, understandable statuses, and relevant actions within each record. The goal is to support detailed operational work while keeping the two CRM environments consistent.

juJutsu.description: Website redesign for a German jujitsu school, focused on helping visitors find a suitable class and book a session online. I took the project from identifying problems in the existing website to building a functional experience in Base44 within three days.
juJutsu.coverAlt: MacBook Pro showing the Ju-Jutsu⁺ trial lesson booking: a progress bar, an October calendar and the free time slots for the selected day, over a line drawing of a pagoda

overview.label: Overview
overview.lead: From a local business problem to a working website.
overview.body:
I selected Ju-Jutsu⁺ after reviewing its existing website and identifying opportunities to improve class discovery and booking. The school’s offering was buried in lengthy content, while the schedule was difficult to navigate and visitors could not book a lesson online.

My work covered defining the concept, restructuring content, planning the user flow, and implementing the website in Base44. I focused on connecting the information prospective students need with the actions they want to take: explore classes, find a suitable time and location, and book a session.

promptToWebsite.caption: From prompt to website
promptToWebsite.alt: Base44 editor on a MacBook Pro: the prompt that describes the Ju-Jutsu⁺ website on the left, the generated homepage with the headline “Komm, wie du bist.” and two people training on the right

goal.label: Goal
goal.lead: Make the first step into training easier.
goal.body:
The challenge was to turn an information-heavy website into a practical tool for choosing and booking classes. Visitors needed a clearer way to understand the school’s offering without reading through multiple sections or searching for relevant schedule details.

I prioritized three tasks:
- finding a class that matches the visitor’s needs
- understanding the training options
- and booking online.

From a business perspective, the aim was to support new student inquiries and reduce the need for manual coordination around schedules and bookings.

design.label: Design
design.lead: Find a class. Explore the options. Book a session.

schedule.title: A filterable training schedule
schedule.body: I introduced a structured timetable with filters for class category, age group, and city. This gives visitors a way to narrow down the available options and focus on sessions relevant to them.

booking.title: Online lesson booking
booking.body: I added a booking flow to give visitors a direct next step after exploring classes. Bringing booking into the website connects class discovery with taking action, rather than leaving visitors to arrange everything through a separate conversation.

assistant.title: Bilingual AI assistance
assistant.body: I integrated an AI assistant with English and Ukrainian support, adding a conversational way to ask questions while exploring the website.

content.title: Clearer content and visual hierarchy
content.body: I shortened lengthy descriptions and reorganized information into scannable sections and cards. A clearer visual hierarchy highlights key details, helping visitors explore training options and find relevant information more easily.

classDiscovery.caption: Class Discovery
classDiscovery.alt: Weekly training schedule from Monday to Friday, filtered by city and course, with one card per class showing its time and location

bookingFlow.caption: Booking Flow
bookingFlow.alt: Booking step “Termin wählen”: a progress bar, an October calendar and the available time slots for the selected day

aiAssistance.caption: AI Assistance
aiAssistance.alt: Homepage hero with two people training in a dojo and the open chat window of the Ju-Jutsu⁺ AI assistant

contentStructure.caption: Content Structure
contentStructure.alt: Class pages as cards: a photo of children training next to the course name, age group, short description and a button to book a trial lesson

result.label: Result
result.lead: An implemented website in three days.
result.body:
I built and published a functional website combining a filterable training schedule, online booking, and a bilingual AI assistant. The result brings class information and booking into one experience, with a more focused structure around prospective students’ immediate needs.

Using AI-assisted development in Base44, I moved from concept to implementation within a three-day timeframe. This project demonstrates my ability to define a focused scope, prioritize useful features, and carry a website beyond static design into a working product.

filmBudget.description: FilmBudget is a website for a Danish video production company, designed to help potential clients understand services and pricing before requesting a quote. I designed the UX and UI for desktop and mobile, focusing on transparent pricing, clear navigation, and a straightforward inquiry process.
filmBudget.coverAlt: MacBook Pro showing the FilmBudget homepage: the headline “Get instant overview of video prices and create your own film budget online” over a changing reel of sports and film footage
filmBudget.coverCaption: *The live website has since been updated

overview.label: Overview
overview.lead: Connecting business goals with the customer journey.
overview.body: My work covered research, site structure, wireframes, UI design, mobile adaptation, and a reusable UI kit. I applied the client’s existing brand guidelines across English and Danish layouts, organizing the experience around exploring services, understanding costs, and requesting a quote.

goal.label: Goal
goal.lead: Helping clients make an informed first step.
goal.body: Stakeholder interviews and a user survey highlighted three priorities: early access to approximate prices, information that builds trust, and easy contact. I translated these insights into a content hierarchy that brings service options and pricing forward, while keeping the path to an inquiry clear.

research.caption: Research & Analysis
research.alt: Research board with stakeholder interview notes, a competitive analysis, a user journey map, user survey charts and an information architecture sketch

decisions.label: Design Decisions
decisions.lead: Clear pricing. Focused choices. Easy contact.

pricing.title: Pricing with context
pricing.body: Three example-based pricing tiers for each video type help visitors compare options and understand the likely budget.

inquiry.title: A clear path to inquiry
inquiry.body: Prominent calls to action and a short contact form guide visitors toward requesting a quote. The confirmation page explains what happens next.

devices.title: Consistency across devices
devices.body: Mobile layouts prioritize pricing and contact actions, while a reusable UI kit keeps components consistent across pages.

result.label: Result
result.lead: A complete desktop and mobile design.
result.body:
I delivered desktop and mobile designs, English and Danish layouts, and a reusable UI kit for developer handoff.

The scope covered service discovery, pricing, quote requests, and confirmation, alongside supporting company and editorial pages.
I applied the client’s existing visual identity throughout and created a reusable UI kit for consistent page layouts.

designFile.caption: Design file overview
designFile.alt: FilmBudget design file: wireframes, desktop pages in English and Danish, mobile pages and the UI kit

independent.title: Independent Designer
independent.p1: Since 2024, I’ve worked independently with international clients on projects across film production, education, logistics, sports, wellness, and service-based businesses.
independent.p2: My experience includes corporate websites, conversion-focused landing pages, multi-screen web applications, CRM-style interfaces, dashboards.
independent.p3: Depending on the project, I work across information architecture, user flows, wireframes, responsive UI, design systems, reusable components, multilingual interfaces, developer handoff, and Webflow/Framer implementation. I also collaborate directly with clients and developers, adapt existing brand systems, and use AI-assisted development to turn selected concepts into functional prototypes.
